title: Two Columns Changed to Vertical List

illustrates.quote: c. When multi-column lists have some items bulleted, transcribe them vertically.

blocks.text: This is his wish list from the Louis L’Amour collection. Bulleted items are out of stock.
blocks.features: Introductory sentence above the two-column list.
Two side-by-side columns of book/story titles, three per column; four of the six titles carry a small solid round bullet ('out of stock'); two are unbulleted.

print.notes: Items listed in print's own column-major reading order (left column top-to-bottom, then right column top-to-bottom), matching the vertical order the braille transcription uses.
print.printFeatures: Boxed illustration; italic introductory sentence; two columns of titles, four marked with a small solid round bullet.

braille.notes: The introductory sentence (lines 1-2) precedes a blank line, then the six titles are transcribed as a single vertical column (lines 4-9) preserving the print's left-column-then-right-column order exactly, per 8.7.1.c; each bulleted title keeps the '_4' dot-bullet symbol in cell 1, unbulleted titles begin directly with the capital sign in cell 1.

resolution: braille.lines byte-identical between A and B. "Louis L’Amour": confirmed curly apostrophe (’, U+2019) directly against the PDF page image (p. 205) — B was right, A’s straight apostrophe (') was a retyping slip; fixed here. Item marker/column structure (already A’s own clean {marker:’•’|null, level, text} shape, columns:2, column-major order) confirmed correct against the same page image and kept as-is.
